current.text: Portland's projected starting five includes Camara at forward, with Lillard, Morant, Avdija and Clingan.
Portland has very thin forward depth. Avdija and Camara are basically its only forwards.
Portland likely needs him for about 34 minutes a night. His minutes should stay solid, and he needs 30 or more for fantasy value.
Portland added several on-ball guards (Lillard, Morant, Henderson), so his usage will probably drop.
His shooting was poor for most of last season and only improved in the final six weeks. His steals were also down.
A rank around 101 is far too high for him. Experts put him in tier 7 among small forwards and see him as little more than a steals source.
Portland has three back-to-backs in the fantasy playoffs and a five-game week starting February 8.

durable.text: He is a point-of-attack defender, the only real one on Portland's roster.
Steals are his best category. Threes are his only other plus category, and neither is a league outlier.
His shooting runs in peaks and valleys, and he has weak ball handling.
He is a poor finisher, which lowers the assist conversion of the guards who pass to him.

note: Camara is an endgame or waiver-level forward for us. Yahoo ranks him 106 with an average cost of 1.0 USD, ESPN ranks him 132 at 0 USD, and he went for 4 USD in our last auction. The experts say paying even that is too much now that Portland's guards will take his usage, so take him only for 1 USD as a steals and threes filler (projected 1.2 STL and 2.0 3PM per game). He has no flagged weak category, so he fits any build. Early in the season, check that he keeps 30 or more minutes and that his FG% stays near the 44% to 45% projection.
